feature: Two copies of the same picture get told apart
summary: Drop one file into a document twice and the second layer arrives as "Hero banner 2" instead of a second row reading "Hero banner". The first copy keeps the plain file name, and a name you typed yourself is never renumbered.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on. You need any image file in the Finder.

try.do: Open any picture, then drag an image file in from the Finder and drop it on the canvas.
Read the top row of the Layers list: it should be the file's name with no number on it.
Drag the same file in again and drop it somewhere else.
Read the Layers list: the new row carries a 2 and the first row is untouched.
Drop it a third time and confirm the number counts on.
Double click the top row and type a name of your own, then drop the file once more.
Confirm your typed name is still exactly what you typed.

evaluate: Is a trailing number the right way to tell two copies apart, or would you rather see something about the picture itself?
Does the first copy staying plain feel right, or would you rather every copy carried a number from the start?
When you rename one row and drop the file again, the freed number gets reused rather than counting past it. Does that read as tidy or as confusing?
Screenshots become names like "Screenshot 10.30.45", so a second one reads "Screenshot 10.30.45 2". Is that legible enough in a narrow panel?
rough: A file whose name already ends in a number is doubled up: dropping "icon 2.png" twice gives "icon 2" and "icon 2 2". Rare, and it still tells them apart, so it was left alone rather than guessed at.

Copying a layer and pasting it still gives two identical rows: that goes through a different path with a different right answer (duplicating already says "copy"), so it is filed separately as copying-a-layer-and-pasting-it-gives-the-copy-it.
Verified live in the probe app with Screen Recording granted, so both pictures here are real window captures, not offscreen renders.
